newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian PM names candidate for finance post.
newsitem.headline: Latvian PM names candidate for finance post.

text.p: Latvian Prime Minister Andris Shkele on Wednesday proposed the head of parliament's budget committee Robert Zile as a candidate for the post of finance minister, a government spokesman said.
Zile is a member of the third largest party in the eight-party ruling coalition, Fatherland and Freedom.
The government spokesman quoted Shkele, currently acting finance minister, as saying that Zile was a specialist in finances and knew the process for drawing up and fulfilling the state budget well.
Latvia has been without a finance minister since last October and controversy over the post was the cause of the fall of Shkele's previous administration in January.
Shkele resigned in January after President Guntis Ulmanis called on parliament to reject Shkele's choice of finance minister.
Ulmanis made the call after reports that proposed finance minister Vassily Melnik had been investigated by the prosecutor's office. Melnik was confirmed by parliament but later resigned.
Shkele and Ulmanis also settled their differences and the president recalled Shkele to the premier's post two weeks ago.
The various government parties are to decide on Zile's nomination next week, the government spokesman said.
